acceptance: `_create_exclusive` closes the descriptor when `fdopen` raises. A test proves it without patching the stdlib, or the code is structured so the failure can't leak.
A test drives a failed state download through the existing fake-gh helper and asserts the caller fails closed.
test_isolation.py, test_local_windows_support.py and tests/integration/runs.py use code-owned seams or real environments instead of patching subprocess, os, urllib, socket or time.
Full suite green on 3.11, 3.13 and the Windows job.
description:
The independent review of Theseus PR #32 (v0.2.1) left these gaps open:
- `runner._create_exclusive` leaks the descriptor if `os.fdopen` itself fails after `os.open` succeeds. This is pre-existing; the inline code had the same shape.
- No test covers a failed `gh run download` in the state-download path.
- Stdlib patching remains in tests the v0.2.1 sweep did not touch, because they had not changed since v0.1.6: `tests/unit/.../test_isolation.py`, `test_local_windows_support.py`, and `mock.patch.dict(os.environ, …)` in `tests/integration/runs.py`. A future hosted review of a Theseus promotion that touches those files will flag them, as it flagged test_legacy_transition.py on BenchBox PR #3962.
- The stage_pull_request_diff failure test is skipped when running as root.
